title: Georgetown extends parking relief for shoppers and businesses on Front Street - NewsBreak
text: GEORGETOWN, S.C. (WCBD) – Visitors and residents enjoying the historic charm of Front Street in Georgetown may find it a little easier to shop and dine downtown thanks to an extended parking ordinance passed by city leaders last week. On Wednesday, Georgetown City Council voted to temporarily suspend the two-hour parking limit, aiming to create a more relaxed and accessible experience for visitors exploring the waterfront district. But while the change is meant to ease stress for shoppers, some business owners say foot traffic has been surprisingly slow this summer. “We are in our summer months right now, and we usually have the streets loaded with people,” said Andrea Johnson, owner of Aunny’s Country Kitchen. “It has declined a little bit. It’s steady, but not to the point where we thought it would be this year, you know, because it’s the summertime. People come here for vacation and stuff like that.” City leaders said they saw a notable increase in downtown business activity after initially suspending the meters in June 2024. Still, some shop owners say parking challenges remain — pointing to downtown employees parking in prime spots meant for customers. Despite the slowdowns, some businesses are seeing success including Swamp Fox Tours, which operates in what’s typically considered the offseason. “I suggest people come early before 11 a.m. and catch our first tour, then grab an early lunch,” said owner Kevin Jayroe. “Or, if you come after 2 p.m., there’s usually plenty of parking, and restaurants are still open. Everyone just wants you to come see what they have to offer.” As the ordinance extension remains in place, local shop owners are urging the community to shop small and support local especially as tourism fluctuates. “It’s very important to keep the businesses open,” said Johnson. “We need the support of the locals to keep the business running.” Jayroe echoed the sentiment. “If you don’t support local, you don’t have local,” he said. “If you want to have these great shopping districts and restaurants, you have to get into those places, spend some money, spend time, and get to know them.” The temporary parking ordinance is currently extended through December 31st, and officials say it could be suspended indefinitely if it continues to show a positive impact on downtown business.
